author: kingpanther13
releaseNotes:
v5.1.8 - 2026-11-13
- docs: support current stable firmware only (#583)
  - This server now supports only the current stable Hubitat firmware. On older firmware, update your hub or stay on an older release of this server.
- feat: one save path and one delete path for code create and delete (#579)
  - Installing app or library code is faster, and every code install now returns the new item's `version`.
  - Deleting app, driver or library code no longer goes ahead when its pre-delete backup fails; nothing is deleted and the reply says why.
  - Deleting an app that doesn't exist now says so instead of reporting success, and a delete the hub refuses now returns the hub's reason.
  - Send driver installs one at a time; to install several, use one bulk install.

v5.1.7 - 2026-11-06
- feat: send expectedVersion with code saves and reject unknown tool arguments (#574)
  - App, driver and library code updates check `expectedVersion` before saving, so a stale version is refused before anything is compiled or written, including on the MCP server's own app.
  - Library code updates (`hub_update_library`) now accept `expectedVersion`.
  - Every tool now refuses arguments it does not recognise (for example a misspelled `expectedVersion`) instead of ignoring them. The legacy custom-rule tools are unchanged.
  - When two saves of the same app or driver collide, the update now says to retry instead of suggesting a syntax error.
  - `hub_call_device_command` with `includeState: false` now skips the state read-back.

v5.1.6 - 2026-11-04
- ci: add manual JVM and OS beta lanes (#577)
- fix: read Rule Machine status from its state instead of its status-span markup (#578)
  - Rule Machine: rule tools work on hub platform 2.5.3, which changed how Rule Machine marks a rule's status.
    - `hub_get_app_config` lists disabled actions again.
    - Restoring a rule whose name shows a status, such as "(Required Expression false)", reports success.
    - A refused action edit leaves the rule unchanged.
    - A condition on a device that has no reading yet is accepted when the rule shows current values.
  - Rule Machine: `hub_get_app_config` no longer lists the "Disabled Trigger" heading as a disabled trigger.
  - Rule Machine: restoring a deleted rule that was the only rule on the hub now restores its triggers and actions.

v5.1.5 - 2026-11-03
- fix: native tools take input types from the page; hub_get_app_config reads inputs as form fields (#576)
  - `hub_set_rule` can set Rule Machine's "Certain Time (and optional date)" trigger with a date, so a rule can fire once on a given day; dates are `yyyy-MM-dd`.
  - `hub_set_rule` and `hub_set_native_app` accept every input type an app page declares, including date, email, phone, menu and file-text inputs; a download-text input reads back its file name and content.
  - `hub_get_app_config` shows each input the way the form tools do, plus an app's child devices, mode restriction, external links and download content, and the app type's namespace and name (also in summary mode).
  - Native app and rule forms refuse Done, Next and page links when a field fails the page's own checks (required, number range, pattern, email), as the Hubitat page does.
  - Installing or saving an app through MCP no longer stores a menu's default option, or a device picker's placeholder default, as if it had been picked.

v5.1.4 - 2026-11-02
- fix: Rule Machine edits and restores keep a blank time setting; load-limiter and PR Guard follow-ups (#573)
  - Fixed editing and restoring a Rule Machine rule that has an unused time field: edits failed to save their pre-edit backup, and restoring the backup failed and left the rule stopped.
  - With the automatic reset of the hub's app runtime statistics turned off, a write refused by the hub's load limiter now also says it may have run some steps and to check its target before calling it again.
  - Bug reports from `hub_report_issue` now show whether the automatic reset is on.

v5.1.3 - 2026-11-02
- build(deps): bump gradle/actions from 6.4.0 to 6.4.1 in the github-actions group ([#571](https://github.com/kingpanther13/Hubitat-local-MCP-server/pull/571), @app/dependabot)
- fix: the server resets the hub's app runtime statistics itself before the per-app load limiter trips (#570)
  - The server now keeps itself clear of the hub's per-app load limiter: it watches its own busy time and resets the hub's app runtime statistics before "generates excessive hub load" can refuse a call, and if a refusal still gets through it resets and repeats the call where that is safe. Long sessions no longer hit that error or the throttling that came with it.
  - The reset clears the hub's Logs › App Stats numbers for every app, not only this one (the hub has no per-app reset). To keep App Stats intact, turn off "Reset the hub's app runtime statistics automatically" under Advanced settings (on by default); the automatic reset also stays off while the Write master is off.
  - `hub_delete_logs` gains `mode: 'appRuntimeStats'` (with `confirm: true`) to reset the hub's App Stats counters on demand.
  - The hub_get_device_attribute guide says a poll or command waitFor on a credential-named attribute (lock codes, PINs) is refused while Hide passwords and credentials is on.

v5.1.2 - 2026-11-02
- feat: rebuild hub_list_devices on the hub's Devices page list (#568)
  - `hub_list_devices` reads the hub's Devices page: `scope` (`authorized`, `all`, `owned`), typed filters (`disabled`, `staleHours`, `stateFilter`, `changedSince`, label/capability/room), `format` and `cursor` paging. `filter`, `onlyOn`, `detailed` and `offset` are removed; MCP-created virtual devices are `scope='owned'`.
    - Summary, ids and context results need no per-device reads, so large inventories answer in one hub request.
    - Records add `driver`, `protocol`, `linked` and `tags`; `lastActivity` is the page's own timestamp.
  - Credential-named device attributes (lock codes, user codes) are hidden on every device read, including a command's state snapshot and event rows, while Hide passwords and credentials is on; a hidden preference value echoed back in an update is refused, and a `stateFilter`, poll or `waitFor` on a hidden attribute is refused.
  - `hub_update_device` sends an enable before data values and a disable after them, so both land, and refuses data values for a disabled device unless `enabled: true` comes with them.
  - `hub_list_devices` names devices whose page entry cannot answer a filter in `metadataUnavailableIds`, and a cursor past the end returns an empty page.
  - Backup retention is a plain FIFO: when all MCP backups together exceed the storage budget, the oldest go first across every item and kind (only the backup being taken and an active restore target are exempt), so a live rule's earlier restore points survive its later edits.

v5.1.1 - 2026-10-30
- feat: rebuild hub_update_device on the device page's native saves (#567)
  - `hub_update_device` now takes `fields` and `preferences`: put device settings such as label, room, tags or showOnHome inside `fields`. `hub_get_device(mode='configuration')` lists every field with its type, current value and whether the device offers it.
    - Device Info changes save in one request and preferences in another, the way the device page saves them; mixed updates are about twice as fast.
    - `room` accepts a room name or id; a number is always an id, and text matches a name first.
    - Settings that already had the requested value are reported as `unchanged` instead of as changes.
  - `hub_create_device` sets the requested label as part of creating the device.
  - New setting: Hide passwords and credentials in MCP responses (ON by default). Turn it off to let the AI read stored passwords and credential-named values.
    - A hidden value sent back in an update is refused, so the stored password or code is never overwritten.
    - More names count as credentials (PINs and codes such as `userPin`, `alarmCode`, `installerCode`), and Rule Machine local variables and device preferences and data named that way (`doorCode`, `alarmPin`) are hidden too.
  - `hub_get_rule_health` reports an unknown app id as not found.
  - `hub_get_app_config` shows each setting's saved value on the page instead of the app's default.
  - Dashboard PINs are hidden while Hide passwords and credentials is on; updating a dashboard from a read keeps its PIN.

v5.1.0 - 2026-10-29
- feat: rebuild hub_set_native_app on the native form engine (#563)
  - Native apps: `hub_set_native_app` now works like `hub_set_rule`: create an app, update its fields, or step through its own pages (`operation` create, update, form). It covers every built-in classic app and user or community apps too. The old parameter names are gone; the tool explains its three operations when called without one. Inputs you leave unset keep their page defaults, a sub-page can be edited in one call, and a refused create leaves nothing behind.
  - Removed tool: `hub_list_app_pages`. Its job moved into `hub_get_app_config`, whose result now lists the pages a page links to under `page.hrefs`; read the default page first and pass a linked page as `pageName`.
  - `hub_get_app_config` with `includeSettings` now hides password values on every page of an app and settings whose names look like credentials. OAuth access tokens follow the "Hide access tokens in MCP responses" setting and are always hidden from per-client tokens.
  - Backups: pre-edit snapshots no longer store password-typed settings; a restore keeps the live password in place and tells you which passwords to re-enter when an app is recreated. When the backup storage budget is full, the oldest backups are removed first and the newest backup of each app or rule is always kept; the "Prioritize the first snapshot when pruning backups" setting is now "Take a fresh snapshot before every edit", which is what it did.
  - Rule Machine: `hub_set_rule` refuses a batch that deletes or edits a row it already deleted before any change, and accepts retargeting an IF and deleting its old condition in one batch; `hub_call_rule` start/stop messages describe exactly what Rule Machine does.
